name: DSP (Demonstrate-Search-Predict)
executive_summary: A framework composing retrieval and language-model calls into multi-step pipelines via declarative operators — Demonstrate, Search, Predict — the direct architectural predecessor to DSPy, from the same research group.
description: Precedes and directly motivates DSPy (already in this catalog): DSP established the core idea of treating retrieval-and-generation pipelines as compositions of a small number of declarative, reusable operators rather than hand-chained prompt strings, specifically for knowledge-intensive NLP where a single retrieve-then-read step is often insufficient (e.g. multi-hop questions needing several rounds of retrieval interleaved with reasoning). DSPy generalized DSP's operators into a broader programming model with automatic compilation/optimization (teleprompters); DSP itself is the earlier, narrower system focused specifically on the demonstrate/search/predict pattern for retrieval-augmented pipelines. Reported substantially outperforming both a vanilla retrieve-then-read pipeline and the contemporary retrieval-and-reasoning state of the art on multiple knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks.
when_to_use: Multi-hop, knowledge-intensive QA pipelines needing several interleaved rounds of retrieval and reasoning, where a single retrieve-then-generate pass (plain RAG) is insufficient.
Historical/architectural context for understanding what DSPy generalized from, when deciding whether DSPy's fuller compilation machinery is needed or DSP's narrower pattern suffices.
when_not_to_use: Single-hop retrieval tasks where plain RAG's one retrieve-then-generate pass already suffices — DSP's multi-step composition is unnecessary overhead.
New projects with no reason to prefer DSP's narrower operator set over DSPy's more general, actively-maintained successor framework.
known_pitfalls: Superseded in practice by DSPy for most new work, which generalizes DSP's operators and adds automatic compilation — DSP is primarily relevant now for understanding the lineage rather than as a first choice for new systems.

primary_source.authors: Khattab, Santhanam, Li, Hall, Liang, Potts, Zaharia
primary_source.title: Demonstrate-Search-Predict: Composing Retrieval and Language Models for Knowledge-Intensive NLP
